Definition: from G1722 and G2904; strong in a thing (masterful), i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) self-controlled (in appetite, etc.):--temperate.
BiblicalUsage: An elder must be temperate in Titus 1:8 — sober, just, holy, self-controlled, a lover of hospitality and of good men.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe leadership in the church is proved by self-mastery first, and the temperate man is the one others can safely follow.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
